scope: 2022 rebuilt research pipeline; legacy databases and historical artifacts are not certified as repaired

findings.detail: Shared parsing now separates docked bikes, free docks and service flags. Historical inventory products and the legacy database have not all been rebuilt.
The 2022 aggregate counts arrivals using their own end timestamps; invalid arrivals do not discard valid departures. Legacy rounded timestamps remain outside this reference run.
The legacy duration conversion was corrected to seconds. Earlier derived datasets were not regenerated; the rebuilt 2022 pipeline uses explicit end timestamps.
The shared snapshot parser retains all source timestamps and flags, and the historical audit reads complete files. A complete production inventory time-series database remains outside this rebuild.
Models predict recorded departures. Inventory forecasts and model-based empty/full alerts remain unavailable.
The current feature pipeline was trained and evaluated again. Candidate caches record code/data fingerprints, parameters and package versions; old scores remain historical.
Exact UTC lags use completed hours with explicit issue and target times. Actual live collection latency has not been measured or validated.
All candidates and both selected models are serialized with contracts. Reloaded validation predictions match within 1e-12; no tree importance is claimed for the selected linear models.
The model cohort requires year-round source IDs and stable coordinates. Network coverage and zero-fill assumptions are explicit; physical station continuity and operating hours remain unproven.
Unvalidated GIS IDs are no longer silently accepted as service IDs. The rebuild uses trip-origin coordinates, but a verified cross-year station identity crosswalk is still missing.

Seven trained model families and three baselines now share the same chronological evaluation rows. Rolling-origin, cold-start and prospective validation remain outstanding; the historical test period has been inspected before.
Last completed hour, target-aligned yesterday and target-aligned last-week baselines are named explicitly and evaluated on identical rows.
Installed versions are pinned in constraints-rebuilt.txt and recorded in model metadata. Cross-platform clean-environment reproducibility is not yet certified; existing deprecation warnings remain.
Current execution, source-time semantics, limitations and model comparison are documented. This does not close every inline documentation gap in the older modules.
Legacy and rebuilt workflows coexist. Broad removal of unused scaffolding and consolidation of duplicate implementations have not been completed.
The rebuilt app renders its own tested charts and static model exports. The legacy SDK and original explorer contract have not been fully revalidated.
Current pages use only rebuilt model exports and exclude obsolete production scores. Older artifacts remain on disk and are not certified for use.
Redundant local outputs have not been deleted. Source archives are retained; disk cleanup still needs a scoped review.
Maintained guides describe the current workflow. Historical assessment inputs and generated audit reports are separate from project documentation; model results are generated from the published run.
The rebuild records source hashes, dependencies, contracts and generated artifact hashes. No PostgreSQL migration, isolated database integration run or live deployment has been validated.

Real hourly ERA5 weather is joined for descriptive usage comparisons. Counts remain recorded trips because the 2022 CSVs lack a reliable customer/operator flag; neither latent demand nor a causal rain effect is established.
Every candidate uses the same nonnegative postprocessing for evaluation and web exports. Selected exports and all-model metrics were independently reconciled.
Python tests, Ruff, mypy and frontend checks are available. Consult the latest check output or CI run for their status; this assessment is not a live CI indicator.
